query: I am investigating the impact of chemical short-range order (SRO) on the thermal conductivity of concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys. Specifically, I need a hypothesis regarding whether SRO formation typically enhances or suppresses lattice heat transport, along with the supporting physical mechanisms. Please outline the expected boundary conditions and propose a falsification experiment to distinguish between scattering-dominated and ordering-dominated transport regimes.

generation.hypothesis: Chemical short-range order (SRO) in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) typically suppresses lattice thermal conductivity at low-to-moderate temperatures (<1000 K) by introducing diffuse antiphase boundaries (DAPBs) that scatter phonons, but this suppression diminishes at high temperatures (>1500 K) where thermal fluctuations disrupt SRO and phonon-phonon Umklapp scattering dominates. The mechanism involves SRO-induced local chemical ordering creating energy barriers for dislocation glide (strengthening) and simultaneously acting as phonon scattering centers, with the thermal conductivity reduction being most pronounced when SRO is stable and long-range order is absent.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloy (e.g., MoNbTaW) in a random solid solution (RSS) state with no long-range order, exhibiting intrinsic lattice thermal conductivity determined by mass disorder and phonon-phonon scattering.
generation.intervention: Induce chemical short-range order (SRO) through controlled annealing at intermediate temperatures (e.g., 800 K) where SRO is energetically favorable but long-range ordering is suppressed.
generation.conditions: Temperature range: 300 K to 2000 K; Alloy system: BCC refractory HEAs (MoNbTaW, NbMoTaW); SRO state: Equilibrium SRO at 800 K vs. random solid solution; Timescale: Fast deformation/transport where SRO state remains static during measurement.
generation.structural_mediator: Diffuse antiphase boundaries (DAPBs) formed at SRO domain interfaces; Local chemical ordering clusters that create potential fluctuations for phonon scattering.
generation.mechanism: At low temperatures, SRO creates DAPBs that scatter phonons (reducing thermal conductivity) and impede dislocation motion (increasing strength). At high temperatures, thermal energy disrupts SRO, reducing DAPB density and phonon scattering, allowing Umklapp processes to dominate. The strengthening effect of SRO on dislocations (via DAPB formation energy) correlates with phonon scattering intensity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Thermal conductivity will be lower in SRO-ordered samples compared to random solid solutions at temperatures <1000 K, with the difference decreasing as temperature increases and vanishing above ~1500 K. The suppression magnitude will correlate with SRO strength (measured by short-range order parameter).
generation.baseline: Random solid solution (RSS) RHEA with thermal conductivity determined by mass disorder scattering and intrinsic phonon-phonon interactions.
generation.boundary: Effect is significant only when SRO is stable (T < T_SRO_disruption); negligible when long-range order forms or when T > T_SRO_disruption; most pronounced in BCC RHEAs with strong SRO driving force (e.g., MoNbTaW).
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative magnitude of thermal conductivity suppression depends on specific alloy composition, SRO correlation length, and measurement technique. The transition temperature where SRO effects vanish may vary by alloy system. Experimental verification of SRO state and its correlation with thermal conductivity is challenging due to similar length scales of SRO and phonon mean free paths.
generation.falsification_experiment: Prepare two sets of MoNbTaW RHEA samples: (1) Random solid solution (quenched from high temperature), (2) SRO-ordered (annealed at 800 K for 24h, then quenched). Measure thermal conductivity using laser flash analysis across 300-2000 K range. Simultaneously characterize SRO using high-energy X-ray diffraction (pair distribution function analysis) and atom probe tomography. Falsification criterion: If thermal conductivity of SRO sample is equal to or higher than RSS sample at any temperature <1000 K, or if no correlation exists between SRO strength (measured by order parameter) and thermal conductivity reduction, the hypothesis is falsified. Additionally, if thermal conductivity suppression persists above 1500 K when SRO is confirmed to be disrupted, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) are designed for high elevated-temperature strength, with both edge and screw dislocations playing an important role for plastic deformation. However, they can also display a significant energetic driving force for chemical short-range ordering (SRO). Here, we investigate mechanisms underlying the mobilities of screw and edge dislocations in the body-centered cubic MoNbTaW RHEA over a wide temperature range using extensive molecular dynamics simulations based on a highly-accurate machine-learning interatomic potential. Further, we specifically evaluate how these mechanisms are affected by the presence of SRO. The mobility of edge dislocations is found to be enhanced by the presence of SRO, whereas the rate of double-kink nucleation in the motion of screw dislocations is reduced, although this influence of SRO appears to be attenuated at increasing temperature. Independent of the presence of SRO, a cross-slip locking mechanism is observed for the motion of screws, which provides for extra strengthening for refractory high-entropy alloy system.

Machine-learning interatomic potential

In this section, we discuss the results of the development of the interatomic-potential model used to enable the application of MD simulations of dislocation properties in bcc MoNbTaW. We employ the general framework of machine-learning (ML)-based approaches, which have emerged recently as a systematic framework to develop potentials with accuracies near that of the underlying DFT calculations for elemental and multicomponent systems [24] , [44] – [46] . Here, using training data reported previously [24] for elemental, binary, ternary, and quaternary systems in Nb–Ta–Mo–W, we developed a potential for the MoNbTaW RHEA based on the moment tensor potential (MTP) formalism, which has been found to feature an excellent balance between accuracy and computational cost [46] .
